rationale: VERIFY_PY10. DENYLISTED_SYMBOL_NAMES gated a `def`/`class` name, which is the one position where the gate could not help: if the grammar produced the node, the name IS a declaration. `super` is a legal method name — django's BlockNode has one at django/template/loader_tags.py:71 and `{{ block.super }}` is its documented template API — and the gate skipped the whole function_definition branch, so not only the symbol but also `ctx.currentFunction` and the exit frame that restores it. The walk then descended into the method with currentFunction undefined and currentClass set, which is the shape of a class body, and four things followed: the method symbol was lost, its method LOCAL was published as a class member, `extractMemberUses` (a second walk, no denylist) emitted `uses` edges naming a symbol that was never published, and `calls` edges were sourced to the class instead of the method. Measured blast radius over all 5,364 code-bearing corpus files: exactly one declaration in the whole corpus is named anything in that set, and it is this `super`. The controls `direct`, `cls`, `self` and `this` are ordinary identifiers that were in the removed set and must still publish — a fixture pinning only the defect is satisfiable by refusing every removed name, which is the over-correction this one is written against. `None`, `True` and `False` are deliberately ABSENT: they are python keywords, so `def None(self)` and `def True(self)` are SyntaxErrors per CPython's own `ast`, the grammar returned an ERROR node with no identifier for both, and the denylist probe independently measured 0 declarations with those names across all 5,364 corpus files. Two drafts of this fixture declared one of them and were corrected by the parser both times.

expectRelationships.comment: the LOSS: django's BlockNode.super had no symbol, so it had no containment either
control: a method named `cls` is an ordinary declaration
control: `def self(self)` is legal — `self` is not a keyword, and the grammar parses it as an ordinary function_definition
control: `this` is a JS-ism but a legal python identifier, and a legal method name
control: the ordinary case the gate was never about
the MISATTRIBUTION: this call is in `super`'s body, so `super` is the source. Pre-fix it was sourced to the class `Holder`
and the DANGLING half: `uses super -> scratch` named a symbol that did not exist, because the local was published as a member while the method was not

forbidRelationships.comment: the FABRICATION: `scratch` is a local of `super`, not a member of Holder. A mis-scoped method body reaches the class-body Property branch and publishes its locals as members
the MISATTRIBUTION, forbidden form: with `super` unpublished the body walked at class scope, so the call was sourced to the CLASS
same, second site — two sites so a fix that re-attributes only the first cannot pass

forbidSymbols.name: scratch
forbidSymbols.comment: a method local is never a symbol, and certainly never a class member
